title: Unstructured donor-search lower bound
notes: Adversary (useful donor placed last) forces n inspections for every deterministic strategy; uniform prior gives (n+1)/2 expected inspections for every order. Limit theorem for the totally unstructured regime; the four escape channels (prior structure, cheap features, reuse, nonzero miss probability) are the falsifiable structure assumptions.

title: Structural-reminding distance: surprisal additivity over Markov retrieval paths
notes: Additivity of -log over the Markov path product; bridge corollary gives the condition for a cheaper two-hop route. Operational theorem about retrieval probability under a stated kernel; explicitly NOT a claim that human neural distance is literal metric geometry. Residual: history-dependent kernels make edge costs non-constant.

title: Adaptive-submodular donor coverage (Golovin-Krause 2011; Sviridenko 2004)

hostile.instance: Two donors {A,B}, one target lemma: A supplies a technique, B an invariant, each alone worthless (f=0,0), together sufficient (f({A,B})=1). Marginal of B rises 0->1 after reading A.
hostile.kills: Adaptive submodularity (increasing marginal) and with it the greedy 1-1/e-style / log-competitive guarantee; parent guarantee invalid in this configuration, requiring joint set-level search or pair-as-item re-registration.

parents.cite: Golovin & Krause 2011, Adaptive Submodularity: Theory and Applications in Active Learning and Stochastic Optimization, JAIR 42
Sviridenko 2004, A note on maximizing a submodular set function subject to a knapsack constraint, Operations Research Letters 32(1)

notes: Adaptive monotone + adaptive submodular => adaptive greedy near-optimality over the registered constraint class (budgeted 1-1/e-style; log(1/p*)-competitive min-cost cover); nonadaptive knapsack => 1-1/e via partial enumeration. Both JAIR fetch attempts returned HTTP 404, so parent-side constants carry PARENT_STATEMENT_UNVERIFIED_TEXT.

title: Hierarchical donor search (Bubeck-Munos-Stoltz-Szepesvari 2011 HOO/X-armed)

hostile.instance: 1-D bandit X=[0,1], dissimilarity l=|x-y|, f=1/2 on [0,1-delta], f(1)=1: the single optimum sits at maximal distance from the broad mediocre shelf; any Lipschitz constant valid across the jump (nu>=1/(2delta)) makes optimism vacuous, any shelf-fit constant makes the bound invalid at x=1. The optimum shares a hidden structural attribute with the target (Higgs-style donor) that l does not measure.
hostile.kills: The chosen dissimilarity l (and any router/hierarchical tree built on it), i.e. the validity of the local-Lipschitz assumption under l - NOT the existence of remote analogy and not the parent theorem, which conditions on a correct dissimilarity.

parents.cite: Bubeck, Munos, Stoltz & Szepesvari 2011, X-Armed Bandits, JMLR 12

notes: Abstract-level claims verified against the JMLR page at freeze time (generic measurable arm space; locally Lipschitz w.r.t. a known dissimilarity; expected regret bounded up to a logarithmic factor by sqrt(n); dimension-independent growth; minimax optimality for metric dissimilarity). Body-level forms (nu/rho parametrization, Assumption 2 on the well-behaved covering tree, near-optimality dimension) carry PARENT_STATEMENT_UNVERIFIED_TEXT. Hostile mandates dissimilarity validation (held-out values vs l-neighbors) before HOO-style routing.

title: Successive-depth allocation (Jamieson-Talwalkar 2016 successive halving)

hostile.instance: K=2 donors, one elimination round: donor A has small value epsilon visible at any depth; donor B* has true value 1 but its depth-r estimate is 0 for all r < d* (signal only at full reconstruction depth). Round 1 runs at depth d1 < d*, SH keeps the top 1 arm = A, B* is discarded deterministically for any halving schedule that does not reach d* before elimination.
hostile.kills: The premise that the best arm is separated the right way at every resource level SH reaches (registered-model applicability of SH to late-blooming donors), not the parent theorem itself.

parents.cite: Jamieson & Talwalkar 2016, Non-stochastic Best Arm Identification and Hyperband Applications, ICML PMLR 51

notes: SH allocates geometrically larger reading budgets to survivors; within its registered model (fixed budget, estimates concentrated at allocated depths, best arm separated at those depths) it is near-optimal up to logarithmic factors. Source page not fetched; exact theorem statement carries PARENT_STATEMENT_UNVERIFIED_TEXT. Mitigation registered: frozen exploration / late-bloomer lane (issue #221), reported with its cost.

title: Cross-atom donor amortization: read-once-map-many average cost identity
notes: Average cost per atom = C_d/m + (1/m)sum(c_i) versus C_d + (1/m)sum(c_i) under per-atom rereading; saving (1-1/m)C_d per atom. Dominance condition: C_d large relative to mapping costs and realized reuse m'>=2 (m'=1 leaves C_d as pure overhead). Load-bearing architecture rule: never reread the same discipline independently per atom; realized m' is measurable via the motif store.

title: Exploration mass necessary for unmodelled remote donors (top-k router limit)
notes: Any deterministic top-k router that never inspects outside its predicted set is defeated by an adversary placing the only useful donor outside the realizable inspection set (miss with probability 1; randomized routers get strictly positive miss probability). Fork: coverage theorem under explicit structure assumptions OR nonzero exploration mass over under-modelled/far regions. Explicitly does NOT make uniform random search efficient (T55 rate); use novelty/diversity/uncertainty-guided exploration and report its cost (budget share, out-of-set inspections, exploration-found vs prediction-found useful donors).

title: Rational metaresearch / VOC stopping (Russell-Wefald 1991; Hay-Russell-Tolpin-Shimony 2012)

parents.cite: Russell & Wefald 1991, principles of metareasoning (Do the Right Thing / Artificial Intelligence 49)
Hay, Russell, Tolpin & Shimony 2012, selecting computations under limited resources

notes: Metalevel VOC = expected downstream decision improvement minus reading/mapping/proof cost; continue while positive, stop/redirect at nonpositive, under the frozen metalevel model.
